subject: Clarify: default log storage — examples of requests vs outputs and deletion evidence
raw_thread:

Cc: ops@apexfin.com

Subject: Quick question on what you 'keep' by default

Mina —

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. One compliance item came up internally: can you show concrete examples of what Redwood stores by default for a typical text generation request? The legal team wants an explicit list like: user request input (raw prompt), intermediate tokens/streamed buffers, final model output, KV cache, and any derived indexing artifacts. They also want to know: when a customer requests deletion, what evidence can Redwood provide that items were erased (example logs, purge job IDs, timestamps)?

We are early in procurement but this will be gating for our legal/compliance signoff. Appreciate short examples and a pointer to the deletion evidence workflow.

—Sanjay
Director, Cloud Ops, Apex Financial

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@apexfin.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what you 'keep' by default

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks — good question and exactly the sort of concrete examples we share with procurement teams. Below is a concise breakdown (examples reflect defaults for our Hosted API in the US region; Dedicated/Private options can change residency and access controls).

What Redwood stores by default (examples):
- User request input (raw prompt): stored as a request record tied to a request_id for 45 days by default in hosted (customer can request shorter retention). Example record: request_id=R-20260624-84, stored fields: timestamp, client_ip (redacted per privacy), prompt_text.
- Streamed buffers/intermediate tokens: ephemeral streams are held in-memory and short-lived disk caches for the duration of the session and are not persisted to long-term logs; when streaming completes we only persist the final output artifact unless the customer opts into session transcripts.
- Final model output: stored as an output artifact associated with the request_id and model_version. Default horizon: 45 days for hosted; outputs are what we typically show in audit snapshots. Example output record: output_id=O-20260624-84, model=gpt-redwood-3, tokens=278.
- KV cache / runtime working set: runtime caches are short-lived and cleared after instance tear-down; we do not index or persist KV cache contents to long-term logs by default.
- Derivative indexing artifacts (embeddings, reranking indices): only created and persisted if a customer enables those features. If enabled, persistence location and retention follow the configured index lifecycle (we include explicit retention settings in the console).

Deletion and evidence: how we demonstrate erasure
- Erasure request flow: customer opens ticket or uses the console to request deletion -> we validate scope (account, project, or specific request_ids) -> schedule purge job across storage partitions -> record purge_job_id.
- Evidence artifacts we provide: purge_job_id (e.g., PJ-20260625-77), timestamp of completion, list of request_ids affected, storage shard identifiers (opaque), and a signed digest that indicates job completion. Example evidence bundle: {purge_job_id:PJ-20260625-77, completed_at:2026-06-25T02:11:05Z, request_ids:[R-20260624-84, R-20260624-85]}.
- Audit trail availability: for hosted customers we can surface the audit record in the console (or provide as a signed export). For Dedicated/Private we deliver the same artifacts via the customer-managed audit endpoint or SFTP per contract.

I'll attach a short retention matrix that summarizes horizons and examples. If you'd like, Karthik can walk through the evidence bundle format in more detail.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Sanjay —

Quick clarifications and a couple of concrete examples you can paste to legal: 
- Example 1 (single prompt, no index): request_id R-20260624-84 -> stored prompt_text, final output O-20260624-84 retained 45 days -> purge job example PJ-20260625-77 removes O-20260624-84 and marks request_id as deleted. Evidence: purge_job_id + completion timestamp + list of removed request_ids.
- Example 2 (customer enabled embeddings): embedding_id E-20260510-12 stored in index IDX-APEX-1 (retention configurable) -> on deletion we run index-compact and issue a purge job that returns deleted index shards + rebuilt CID list. Evidence includes compact job id and index shard manifest.

Operational notes:
- Streaming fragments are not part of the long-term store unless the customer explicitly turns on session recording.
- Logs that show deletion activity (audit.log entries) are retained per our audit retention policy and we can include those entries in the evidence export.
- If Apex needs physical proof for regulatory audit, we can provide a signed CSV of affected IDs and a time-stamped job receipt — we do not provide raw storage paths in hosted mode, but for Dedicated/Private we can provide the full path and verification steps.

If you want a short meeting to walk through a sample evidence bundle, I can set aside 20 minutes.

Thanks,
Karthik
